hard_gates.gate: G3 clean clone: ./erp verify (build, migrate, seed, every test)
hard_gates.evidence:
I ran three full alone verifies (ERP_VERIFY_ALONE=1, through verify-slot.sh) on a fresh clone of 841abb83, with project c-p00-foundation-r23 and ports 20050/20051/20060/20061 set through the environment.

Run 3 passed every test. Slot taken 17:06:23Z, with nothing else of mine running:
- dotnet 1,216, web unit 811, e2e 180, compare 494, build 22. That is 2,723 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, and every count is at or above its minimum.
- The built-ours health check verified all 24 drivers.
- Every ratchet line passed except one: 'verify.cpuSeconds: the verify stages used 26092 processor seconds, maximum 26000' (dotnet 22,202, web 2,864, e2e 927, timing 98). That is 92 s (0.35 %) over, at load mean 9.3 and peak 25. The ratchet also printed 'other work beside the verify 34978 s (57.3 %)'. Under the critic rule, integrators' alone runs measure this maximum, so I report it and do not judge on it.

Run 1 failed only web/src/modules/shell/clientIsolation.test.tsx. Its first test timed out at 30 s and the other 9 cascaded, at load 16 to 23. I stopped run 1 by its PID.

Run 2 failed only gauntlet/compare measured-part.test.mjs 'control C3', judged invalid on StyleRecalcInvalidationTracking, so 493/494 compare tests passed. Its dotnet stage and its e2e stage (180/180, health check 24/24) passed.

Evidence: verify-summary.txt, the logs of runs 1 to 3, run1-kept/, run2-kept/, run3-kept/.

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: my own live attack as tenant A (alnoor) on tenant B (gulfsteel): API, exports, jobs, files
hard_gates.evidence:
attack/attack.mjs (the critic script carried from r22) collected 872 B-only ids and sent, as A:
- all 260 operations with B's ids
- 1,668 documented query-parameter requests
- 1,140 tenant-switch requests (headers, query, cookies)
- 190 export requests, 77 filter requests and 346 path-variant and audit requests.

'B rows unchanged by A attack: true': B's checksums over all 34 tenant tables were identical before and after.

All 138 flagged lines are explained (attack/probe.txt, attack/probe-db.txt):
- 81 audit-record reads with B ids answered byte-identically to a random id (54/54 in the probe).
- 'Gulf Steel' and 'الخليج' are A's own data: 143 and 1,633 alnoor contacts carry them.
- B's tenant id in A's audit log and CSV comes from A's own attack payload: the jobs.jobs and jobs.schedules inserts by admin@alnoor with {tenantId: B}.
- DELETE of B's rate, file and import answered 204, like a random id. B still downloads its file (200, 69 bytes) and reads its rate (200), while A gets 404 on both.

The full tenant export as A now succeeds: 32 files, 14.9 MB. It holds no B id (31 checked), no B canary, no 'gulfsteel' and no B tenant id (attack/full-export.txt).

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: the database role the app uses
hard_gates.evidence:
The app connects as erp_app (ConnectionStrings__App). No erp role is superuser or has BYPASSRLS. All 34 tables with tenant_id have row-level security enabled and forced and a NOT NULL tenant_id, and none is owned by erp_app.

Signed in as erp_app (db-roles-and-app-attack.txt):
- With no tenant set it sees 0 contacts and 0 audit rows. A session-level SET app.tenant_id to B's id also shows 0.
- SET ROLE erp_owner and postgres are denied.
- row_security=off answers 'query would be affected by row-level security policy'.
- NO FORCE and DISABLE RLS answer 'must be owner'.
- CREATE in public and reading pg_authid are denied.

There is no real or double precision column anywhere.

hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions on the real product

attack/revoke-live.txt: the admin removed identity.roles.read from Read-only. The signed-in viewer's next request got 403, and after the permission was restored it got 200.

Browser (browser/walk.log):

- The viewer sees no New button on Roles, and POST role answers 403.

All G2 classes passed in all three verifies.

hard_gates.gate: G1/G2 gate self-check: faults planted in p00's kernel (plants/plants.diff, plants/plant-results.txt)
hard_gates.evidence:
All plant runs went through the verify slot.

L23 was a tenant leak in the kernel list framework, ListBinding.QueryAsync: a static 60 s 'count memo' keyed by list, search and filter, with no tenant. G1ProcessStateTests caught it: 'static Erp.Kernel.Lists.ListTotalMemo.Totals: a read-only field that holds a mutable ConcurrentDictionary ... key it by tenant'.

P23 was a permission fault in SessionAuthenticationHandler: a session's permissions were kept for 5 minutes, so a removed permission kept working. Two gates caught it. The static walk did. G2ReportDataTests also caught it by behaviour, with 2 of 101 G2 tests failing: 'catalogue for [reports.catalog.read, contacts.contacts.read] lists reports [], expected [contacts.contactCard]' and a 403 on tenancy.companyProfile.

P23b was an action without its permission in PermissionAuthorizationHandler: any permission of a module passed every <module>.*.read check. G2PermissionTests.Granting_exactly_one_permission_opens_exactly_the_endpoints_that_declare_it caught it: '[bearer] contacts.contacts.archive: GET /api/contacts/contacts answered 200 (expected 403)'.

This round's p00 change adds no product surface. It only changes the G1 gate's attack names, the marker judge and the list-walk take.

biggest_gap.title: The one-command verify is still slow, unreliable and at its processor-time ceiling: 1 of 3 alone runs passed every test, 8,639 s wall time, 26,092 s against the 26,000 s maximum
biggest_gap.detail:
Every gate held and every p00 test passed in all three runs. What most holds the foundation back is the cost and flakiness of proving it. Every later business module pays this on every integration.

Reliability:
- Two of three alone verifies, each the only verify on the machine, failed on one load-sensitive test outside p00's code.
- Run 1: web clientIsolation.test.tsx timed out at 30 s and cascaded to 10 failures. This happened at load 16 to 23 during the first minutes, when ./erp verify itself starts the web tests, the .NET build, the app image build and the e2e stack together.
- Run 2: the comparison harness's measured-part control C3 was judged invalid on StyleRecalcInvalidationTracking.
- So a critic needs about two to three 2.4-hour runs for one green run. The load that breaks these tests comes from verify's own stage layout, not from other agents.

Wall time:
- Run 3 took 8,639 s against the ratchet's 3,600 s quiet-machine figure.
- The dotnet stage is again paced by the third G1 HTTP share: 1 h against 30 m 7 s, 33 m 13 s and 37 m 56 s for the others. In processor time it is 4,799 s against 2,308 to 3,182 s. The shares are still unbalanced, as in r22.

Cost:
- Processor time was 26,092 s against the 26,000 s maximum, 92 s over in an alone run.
- The next endpoint any piece adds pushes integrations over again.
